name: You are made of stardust
description: Hydrogen was born in the Big Bang. Every heavier element in your body was forged inside a star, and the heaviest ones in supernova explosions. Your atoms are 4.6-billion-year-old cosmic material, and you breathe star-forged carbon with every breath.

hook_variants.template: You are made of stardust. Literally. Here's the chain.
The carbon in your hands was forged in a dying star.
Where did the carbon in your body come from? Hint: not Earth.

sections.text: The Big Bang made hydrogen and helium. That's it. Nothing else.

visual.subtitle: of your body is oxygen — forged in stars

sections.text: Then stars fused them into carbon and oxygen. The stuff your body is built from.
Heavier elements need supernovae. Exploding stars.
A cloud of that stardust formed our solar system. Four point six billion years ago.

visual.title: the twist
visual.body: every breath pulls in carbon forged in stars billions of years before Earth existed

sections.text: Every breath pulls in carbon forged inside a star.
You're not just in the universe. The universe is in you. Follow.

facts.claim: Big Bang nucleosynthesis produced hydrogen, helium and trace lithium; essentially all heavier elements are made later
Stars create heavier elements (up to iron) by nuclear fusion in their cores
Elements heavier than iron are formed by neutron capture processes (s-process, r-process) including in supernovae
Oxygen is about 65% of human body mass
facts.source_name: Wikipedia — Composition of the human body

facts.claim: The Solar System formed about 4.6 billion years ago from the gravitational collapse of a giant molecular cloud
facts.source_name: Wikipedia — Formation and evolution of the Solar System

facts.claim: The quote 'we are made of star-stuff' was popularized by Carl Sagan
